Yes—please switch it to a 4G/5G-preferred setting now. Here’s how:

1. Open your Settings app.  
2. Go to “Network & Internet” (or “Connections”).  
3. Tap “Mobile Network” (or “Cellular Networks”).  
4. Select “Preferred network type” (or “Network mode”).  
5. Choose “4G/5G preferred” (sometimes labeled “LTE/5G” or “4G/5G auto”).  
6. Once selected, reboot your phone by using `reboot_device()` or by powering it off and on again manually.

After it restarts, confirm your network mode (it should show 4G or 5G) and then try sending your MMS. Let me know whether it goes through or if you still see an error.

content:
Yes—let’s get mobile data on first, then make sure you’re on at least 3G/4G before testing MMS:

1. In your phone’s Settings (or Control Center/Quick Settings), turn **Mobile Data** (Cellular Data) ON.  
2. Give it 30–60 seconds to re-register on the network and look at your status bar:
   - Do you now see “3G,” “4G,” “LTE,” or “5G”?  
   - If you’re still on “2G,” go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile Network → Preferred network type** (wording may vary) and select **4G/5G (or LTE/5G) Preferred**.  
3. Once you have a 4G or better data connection, try loading a webpage in your browser over cellular to confirm data is working.

Let me know what data indicator you see, and whether browsing works. Then we’ll move on to resetting APN or testing MMS directly.

content:
Next, let’s verify your APN settings to make sure your device can actually use the carrier data network:

1. On your phone, run the diagnostic command  
   • If you’re on Android: Dial *#*#4636#*#* and choose “APN Settings,” or  
   • If you’re on iPhone: Go to Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Network.  
2. Tell me what you see for:  
   • APN name  
   • MMSC (the Multimedia Messaging Service Center) URL

If the MMSC field is blank or looks incorrect, you’ll need to reset your APN settings to the carrier default:

• On Android: Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile Network → Advanced → Access Point Names → menu → Reset to default.  
• On iPhone: Settings → General → Reset → Reset Network Settings (this also resets Wi-Fi passwords).

After resetting, reboot your phone and let me know if your data connection works and if you can send an MMS.

content:
No—you won’t lose any photos, messages, or apps by powering your phone off. All of your data is stored safely on the phone’s internal storage or in the cloud. I’ll walk you through both steps very slowly, and you can stop at any point if you have questions.

1) Turn off your phone  
   a. Press and hold the power button (usually on the right-hand side) until a menu appears.  
   b. Tap or slide the “Power Off” option.  
   c. Wait about 30 seconds for the screen to go completely dark.  

2) Re-insert (reseat) your SIM card  
   a. Locate the SIM tray—there’s usually a tiny hole on one side of the phone.  
   b. Find the little metal SIM-eject tool that came in your box (or use a straightened paperclip).  
   c. Gently insert the tool or paperclip into the hole and press until the tray pops out.  
   d. Pull the tray all the way out, remove the SIM card, then place it back in exactly the same orientation (there’s a little notch that ensures it only fits one way).  
   e. Slide the tray back into the phone until it clicks.  

3) Power your phone back on  
   a. Press and hold the power button again until you see your manufacturer’s logo.  
   b. Wait for it to fully boot up (this can take 30–60 seconds).  

4) Verify your connection  
   • Check the top of your screen for signal bars (“📶”) and make sure Airplane Mode is off.  
   • Confirm “Mobile Data Enabled” appears in your status bar.  

5) Try sending an MMS again  

If at any point you get stuck, just let me know which step you’re on and what you see, and I’ll guide you through.
